newsitem.title: UK: Greenalls leads brewing stocks higher.
newsitem.headline: Greenalls leads brewing stocks higher.

text.p: Greenalls Plc led the UK brewing sector higher on Tuesday, rebounding from recent underperformance after better-than-expected results from Whitbread Plc, analysts said.

Analysts at Charterhouse Tilney and SocGen repeated "buy" recommendations on Greenalls in the wake of the Whitbread figures, helping send the stock up 17-1/2p at 588-1/2 by 1554 GMT, after earlier touching a five-month high of 590p.
Among other brewing stocks, Bass Plc was up 3-1/2p at 789 and Scottish & Newcastle Plc was up 4-1/2p at 647-1/2.
Analyst Steven Baird at SocGen said he repeated a "buy" recommendation on Greenalls after the Whitbread figures.
"Whitbread has been giving a bullish picture on consumer spending," Baird said.
"Taxes are down, house prices are up and people are spending more money. It's not a return to the mid-eighties but there is a greater change of a feel-good factor emerging."
At Charterhouse analyst Nigel Parson also reiterated a "buy" on Greenalls and said the Whitbread figures were often a good pointer to forthcoming results for the rest of the sector.

"Whitbread kicks off the results season and it is always a good indicator," Parson said. "Whitbread has done very well relative to the rest of the market in recent weeks and Greenalls has been left quite a long way behind."
